gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly identifies the false pointwise truncation estimate: the operator norm must be multiplied by ||x||, with a uniform bound on the stated ball. Its repair and effect match the gold defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify replacing the action of (I-P_N)F on x by its operator norm alone, omitting the input norm factor and thereby invalidating the literal nonasymptotic bound.

component_coverage.gold_component: The estimate omits the factor ||x|| when bounding the truncation action on x.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the correct pointwise operator-norm-times-input-norm estimate and supplies the bounded-ball repair.

component_coverage.gold_component: The displayed literal error bound is false, although the later rate can retain a fixed local multiplicative constant.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives a counterexample showing the numerical inequality is false and prescribes carrying the uniform ball bound into the rate.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 explicitly identifies the invalid transfer from H^s-continuity to continuity in the C supremum topology, gives the same type of compact-domain counterexample for functionals and operators, and supplies the corresponding topology repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the topology mismatch that point-sampling architectures require C-topology continuity while the theorem assumes only H^s-topology continuity, invalidating uniform approximation for both scalar and L²-valued maps.

component_coverage.gold_component: H^s-continuity does not provide the C-supremum continuity required by point-sampling approximation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the exact topology mismatch and demonstrates failure of uniform approximation on a C-compact domain.

component_coverage.gold_component: The same obstruction applies to the operator theorem via an L²-valued construction.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly lifts the scalar counterexample to an operator and states that the universal approximation extension to functionals and operators is false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The premise must be repaired by requiring C-topology continuity or suitable compactness making the topologies agree.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same substantive repair: impose C-topology continuity or H^s-compactness so the required continuity is available.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-017 independently diagnoses the full admissibility failure: the supremum ranges over inputs not guaranteed to lie in D(F), and mollification can leave D(F), making F[x_xi] undefined. This covers the gold's domain-preservation and neighborhood-admissibility concerns, though it presents them through the theorem's admissible-set formulation rather than the exact center-ball argument.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify the failure to ensure that every input at which F is evaluated—including all inputs in the local ball and their mollifications—belongs to the operator domain, so the approximation theorem is not well-defined.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the prediction uses a different formulation and manifestation of the admissibility failure rather than reproducing the center-membership wording.

component_coverage.gold_component: Mollification need not preserve D(F), so F[M_xi x] can be undefined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that x in D(F) does not ensure x_xi is in D(F), and identifies the resulting undefined F[x_xi] evaluations.

component_coverage.gold_component: Membership of only the center does not establish that the whole displayed ball lies in D(F).
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies that the supremum is incorrectly taken over a full L² ball rather than its intersection with the admissible domain and requires restricting the approximation set to admissible inputs.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-018 concerns lack of uniform mollification approximation on a fixed L² ball and the resulting impossibility of uniform network approximation. It does not identify the distinct false same-radius inclusion M_xi(B_r(x*))⊆B_r(x*) or the missing control of the mollified center displacement, so it does not cover this issue.

ISSUE-016 explicitly identifies the reversed quantifier dependence: one xi and one network are asserted for all centers, while the construction fixes a center and depends on it. It gives the same global-versus-center-dependent counterexample and repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both identify that the theorem claims a single finite network and smoothing level uniformly over all centers, although the construction only supports center-dependent choices.

component_coverage.gold_component: The stated quantifier order requires one network to work at every center.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the global quantifier consequence and contrasts it with the center-dependent construction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The global claim is false and only a center-dependent local claim is supported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the identity-on-L² obstruction and states that the globally quantified guarantee is false for allowed operators.

component_coverage.gold_component: The repair must quantify separately over each center and allow center-dependent parameters.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies the required center-dependent repair for xi and network parameters.
